channel.title: Black Girl Gone: A True Crime Podcast
channel.description:
True crime with a new focus...shining a light on the all too often ignored cases of Black women and girls who have gone missing or have fallen victim to murder.
Each episode takes you on a heart wrenching journey through the stories of these women and girls and the families they left behind. Join us as we work to uncover hidden truths and bring the stories of these women to the forefront.
Together we can seek justice for the forgotten and give a voice to the voiceless.
New episodes Now Available Weekly

item.description:

item.title: MURDERED: The Murder Of Tamika Huston
item.description:
In the spring of 2004, twenty-four-year-old Tamika Huston disappeared from Spartanburg, South Carolina. At first, her family hoped she had simply left town. But as days turned into weeks, and weeks into months, it became clear that something was terribly wrong.
An abandoned car, a mysterious ring of keys, and a series of unexpected investigative breakthroughs would ultimately lead detectives to the truth about what happened to Tamika—and expose a calculated effort to conceal her murder.
On this episode of Black Girl Gone, I tell the story of Tamika Huston, the fifteen-month investigation that finally brought her home, and the family who refused to let her be forgotten.

item.title: MURDERED: The Murder Of Anteeatta Swims
item.description:
In June 2021, 35-year-old Anteeatta "Tee" Swims was preparing for a fresh start. After years of trying to save her marriage, she had made the difficult decision to leave her husband and begin a new chapter. But before she had the chance, Tee disappeared.
For two days, her family received strange text messages they knew she hadn't written. Then the truth came to light.
On this episode of Black Girl Gone, I tell the story of Tee Swims, the life she built as a beloved educator, the relationship she fought to save, and the devastating events that ended her life just as she was preparing to walk away.

item.title: MURDERED: The Murder Of Marlisa Wells
item.description:
On January 19, 2008, sixteen-year-old Marlisa Wells was murdered inside the Austell, Georgia home she shared with her grandparents.
Just hours earlier, Marlisa had been making plans for her future. But behind the scenes, she was navigating a secret relationship and what she believed was a life-changing pregnancy. As investigators reconstructed her final hours, they uncovered the evidence that led them to her killer.
In this episode of Black Girl Gone, we tell the story of Marlisa Wells and the devastating tragedy that forever changed her family.

item.title: UNSOLVED: The Murder Of Karitha and Jamaya Carroll
item.description:
In September 2009, 31-year-old Karitha Carroll and her three-year-old daughter, Jamaya, were found murdered inside their home in Cary, Mississippi. What followed was an investigation marked by conflicting theories, controversial decisions, arrests, and a confession that ultimately fell apart. Nearly seventeen years later, no one has been held accountable for their murders.
In this episode of Black Girl Gone, I tell the story of Karitha and Jamaya, and the long search for answers in a case that remains unsolved.

item.title: MURDERED: The Murder Of Felecia Williams
item.description:
On May 16, 2014, 9-year-old Felecia Williams left home to spend the afternoon with someone her family trusted. Less than twenty-four hours later, her body was found in the waters of Tampa Bay.
As investigators searched for answers, they uncovered a web of lies, conflicting stories, and evidence that pointed to the man who had been alone with Felecia during the final hours of her life.
In this episode of Black Girl Gone, we tell the story of Felecia Williams, a little girl known as "Sugarplum," whose life was stolen by someone she should never have been left alone with.

item.title: UNSOLVED: The Murder of Tyeasha Starks
item.description:
On February 20, 2023, 23-year-old Tyeasha Starks went to pick up her young son in Jackson, Tennessee. What should have been a routine custody exchange ended with Tyeasha being shot and killed.
Tyeasha was a devoted mother and college student whose family says she was trying to navigate an increasingly strained co-parenting relationship. In the years since her death, no criminal charges have been filed, and her loved ones continue to seek answers.
On this episode of Black Girl Gone, I tell the story of Tyeasha Starks and the circumstances surrounding her murder.

item.title: SUICIDE OR MURDER: The Mysterious Death Of LaVena Johnson
item.description:
In 2005, 19-year-old Private First Class LaVena Johnson deployed for her first tour of duty in Iraq. She was found shot in a tent 6 weeks after she first arrived for her tour. The Army ruled he death a suicide but her family says she was murdered. LaVena's body showed signs that someone had done something to LaVena despite the Army claiming it was suicide. 16 years later we are still asking what happened to LaVena?
